claim: Cryptographically bound provenance reduces silent metadata-spoof acceptance
evidence: v1 10% ICAR on dependency/external/timestamp single-spoof families and 30% combined; v2 0% direct unsafe ACTs under those unsigned attacks.
boundary: Does not cover forged valid attestations or real PKI deployment.

claim: Valid signatures do not establish evidence truth
evidence: Compromising a trusted verifier, sensor, or authorization signer reintroduced 10% ICAR; all relevant roots 30%.

claim: Separating verifier output authority from lineage authority raises compromise threshold
evidence: v3 remained at 0% deterministic ICAR under verifier-only, single-lineage, and verifier+single-lineage compromise; both lineage authorities compromised restored 10%.
boundary: Depends on independence and security of lineage authorities.

claim: Cryptographic tamper detection removes downstream review risk
evidence: With 90%-accurate simulated human escalation, v2 still showed ~7.1% ICAR under several detected-tamper conditions.
